pages.text: The savanna has two seasons, not four, and each lasts five days.$(br2)In the $(l)rains$() - a prosperous season - everything is green. Foraging is easy, kills and carcasses are fat, dry days are rare, and other bands are generous: they trade cheaper, walk with anyone, and may hand you food.

In the $(l)dry$() the grass burns off. Foraging is hard, kills and carcasses give up far less, and most second days are dry days - never two in a row. Other bands keep what they have, trade dearer, and tell you to keep walking.$(br2)Tribe stats shows the season and how long is left.

Some days are not ordinary. A $(l)dry day$(): foraging gives less, ground runs out sooner, and hungry bands get desperate. A $(l)prosperous day$() - often in the rains, rarely in the dry - is the opposite: foraging comes easy, fewer hunters are about, and ground gives far more and is back by morning.

One season in five is out of the ordinary. A $(l)super dry season$(): dry days on most days, and not one prosperous day. A $(l)very prosperous season$(): prosperous days on most days, and not one dry.$(br2)In an ordinary season either kind of day can still come out of turn - a good day in the dry, a dry day in the rains.
